native_mechanisms: A runner walks each road carrying its notched length and lays a new stick on the far heap equal to the home heap's ember plus that notch (per-edge relaxation dist[u]+w(u,v)).

Every heap throws its sticks in one land-wide simultaneous throw, and a single row read straight across picks each heap's shortest sliver as its new ember while all longer slivers are burned (global synchronous round + per-node min, one value carried forward).

A garrison seals a heap whose ember stopped changing between throws, fixing its distance permanently, refusing incoming sticks, and halting its own runners for good (per-node settle/freeze that prunes work).
core_technique: Synchronous (Jacobi/double-buffered) Bellman-Ford: repeated whole-graph relaxation implemented as a per-node min-reduction over incoming CSR edges, reading only pre-round distances and writing a shadow array, looping until a round changes nothing or n-1 rounds elapse, OpenMP-parallelised.
